dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: Um, pardon me, but could you stay and talk to me for a minute? I'm... kinda scared.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it? What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: I need... Fine, I just need someone to talk to me, really. Radoslaw keeps telling me I was lucky to escape death, but I can't shake off this cold feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: One of the older Lightkeepers told me this a long time ago: "That's how it happens — your body gets colder and colder, and then you realize that no one's talking to you anymore..."

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: "And that's how people leave this world. It doesn't hurt at all, so don't be afraid." ... *sigh* I didn't find that reassuring at all.

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: So, the fact that you're talking to me means that I'm still here... I'm still here, and that's good enough. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: Well, it was a very dangerous op with monsters everywhere... It's a good thing we have pretty good doctors.

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: Mmm... I have to say, my wounds still hurt a bit — my chest, my back... I didn't expect to get hurt this badly. But someone has to step up, and this time, it was my turn.

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: I used to be the one cowering at the back, behind all the guys, and always the first to turn and run when it was time to retreat. But this time, at least, things were different.

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: ...Almost kicked it in exchange, though. Malusha's right: I'm an idiot who has no business on a battlefield.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but I don't have the time right now.

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: That's alright... It's enough that you said that one thing to me. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Lauri
dialogues.text: ...Mmm, you're right. But I don't... dare close my eyes just yet.
